bankroll.verdict: BANKROLL DOES NOT BIND. Mean utilisation is under 1% and even the largest single position used 17% of it. More money buys nothing while concurrency is 1, and asking for money would be asking for the wrong resource.

candidate_supply.reading: 41.9% of flat cycles admitted two or more markets, so candidate supply would support a second slot about two cycles in five. That is a supply measurement, not a P&L one.
candidate_supply.measured_on_flat_cycles_only: while a position is held the selector does not run, so supply during held cycles was never recorded. Supply on flat cycles is not proof of supply on held ones.

concurrency_pnl.why: the frozen concurrency gate already ruled this arm unverifiable: on held cycles select_candidate is never reached, so the admissible universe a second slot would have drawn from was never recorded. Reconstructing it would be an assumption about the very thing being tested.

completion_curve.validation: at the observed 83.42% the curve returns $-0.0742 per dollar-hour against the -$0.0721 measured directly, which is the only check available on it
completion_curve.assumption_that_could_break_it: pair profit is held constant as completion rises, and the marginal completion is probably the harder one -- worse price, thinner book. Every point carries a sensitivity at half the pair profit for that reason.

the_capacity_finding: The slope through the current rung is NEGATIVE: at 83.4% completion the lane runs at $-1.84/day. Scaling multiplies unit economics, it does not repair them, so every axis of growth makes the loss bigger until completion clears break-even at 84.5%. Capacity is not the constraint and capital is not the constraint -- completion is.
read_only: Nothing here proposes a rung. No cap, gate, threshold or concurrency setting moves without the owner's explicit go.
